tagline: Hayfields and stone walls from Webster's cabin to Pierce's homestead.
intro: From the log cabin where Daniel Webster was born, the byway works south through Salisbury and Webster and down into the Contoocook valley. Moss-covered stone walls mark old property lines, the fields beside them have been hayed for more than 200 years, and Mount Kearsarge and Pats Peak are in view. The villages come in clusters of eighteenth- and nineteenth-century churches and town buildings, and the road ends at the Franklin Pierce Homestead in Hillsborough.
The route began in 1976 as one of the state's Bicentennial Yankee Trails. The old printmakers' name is a registered trademark, used with the Currier & Ives Foundation's permission.

moments.title: Daniel Webster Birthplace
moments.text: A two-room log cabin, restored to late 18th-century farm life, where the orator was born in 1782, open on weekends in season.

moments.title: Contoocook Railroad Bridge
moments.text: In Contoocook village the oldest covered railroad bridge in the country crosses the river on a bias, its center pier skewed to match the current.

moments.title: Henniker
moments.text: A stone double-arch bridge of 1835 crosses the Contoocook in a mill town that, in the 19th century, had a sign language of its own.
